payload.summary: Ward Flow's synthetic patient records sit in a public repository under a 2026-08-31 ruling the owner has deferred, not withdrawn
payload.detail: REFRAMED 2026-09-20 after Codex correctly flagged the original wording on PR #2930, and RE-QUEUED the same day with two figures corrected (see the end of this row). The original row was titled around the repository contradicting the 2026-09-01 assume-private ruling. THAT CONTRADICTION IS RESOLVED and must not be re-raised: PR #2927 superseded that ruling in docs/ward-flow-owner-rulings-2026-09-01.md with the owner's 2026-09-20 decision, quoted verbatim - 'i will leave it public for now' - and recorded the first actual measurement (GitHub API: private=false, visibility=public). Leaving the row as written would have taught later sessions to treat a deliberate owner decision as an urgent unresolved defect, which is the same absence-read-as-signal failure this ledger exists to prevent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is the 2026-08-31 ruling, section 5: 'Ward Flow is NOT to be pushed to a public repository as it stands.' The owner has DEFERRED that decision (2026-08-31 community audit, item 9: 'Defer for now - his decision, made knowing the eight invented patient records and three commits of history are public'), and deferred is not withdrawn. Its measured basis has grown since: the UMRNs appear in 16 files today where the ruling recorded 2, and the names in 8 where it recorded 5; its commit figure was right and does not move, at 3. The records are genuinely synthetic - the file header reasons the choice at length and the screens carry a visible synthetic-data marker - and the ruling's point was never that they are real, but that they do not look invented: eight full names, each with a UMRN and a date of birth, in a psychiatrist's public repository. The two options the owner approved at the time remain the options: make the repository private, or replace every name and UMRN wherever they appear and publish a fresh repository with a single initial commit, since publishing a repository publishes its history. NEXT ACTION IS THE OWNER'S, not an assistant's: this row exists to keep the deferral visible, not to reopen a settled decision. FIGURE CORRECTION, 2026-09-20, and it is worth stating because it ran in the dangerous direction: every earlier version of this row - and both ruling documents - recorded 12 files and 4 commits. Measured at HEAD: git grep -l UM10000 gives 16, git grep -l 'Talia Halloway' gives 8, git log --all -S UM100001 on the seed file gives 3. The 12 came from searching for UM100001, THE FIRST RECORD OF EIGHT, which misses the four files carrying one of the other seven UMRNs and not the first (mockup-ward-board-v3.html, patient-and-referral-screens-2026-09-02.md, tests/ui-ward-search.spec.ts, tests/ward-add-patient.dom.test.tsx). A privacy count taken from one specimen of eight understates exposure by construction, and understating it is the direction that makes publishing look safer. The 4 was the opposite error, counting commits that TOUCH ward-patients-seed.ts rather than commits that CARRY the records. Both ruling documents were corrected in the same change and keep the wrong figures visible rather than overwriting them.
